meta_title: Not an Acumatica Alternative: Keep It, Add Voice Ordering
meta_desc: Give the kitchens that skip your Acumatica portal a way to speak each order and check every line. Not an Acumatica alternative: an ordering app beside it.

hero.lead: The chefs who call in every order can send it from an app instead. They say what is needed in the VoiceOrder Solutions app and fix any line that is off before it goes. Acumatica stays your ERP.

problem.h2: If kitchens can log in, why look at an Acumatica competitor?
problem.lead: Often, a distributor who looks at an Acumatica alternative is not trying to leave the ERP. Some may have opened the portal to every account already, and some kitchens phone every order anyway. Here is why the portal alone does not stop the calls.

cards.h3: A login was never the problem
cards.body: Acumatica charges for the apps you run, not for user seats, so giving each kitchen a login carries no seat fee. Even so, some kitchens with a login keep calling.

cards.h3: The portal asks a chef to shop
cards.body: Acumatica's portal shows the catalog with photos, stock on hand and each account's prices, then a cart and a checkout. That suits someone ordering from a desk, less so a chef counting cases at the shelf.

cards.h3: Calls still become typing at your desk
cards.body: When a kitchen phones, texts or leaves a voicemail, someone at your desk types it up as an Acumatica sales order. The portal saves that typing only for kitchens that log in.

features.h2: What your team gets, and why it is not an Acumatica alternative

rows.h3: No catalog, no cart: the chef just says it
rows.body: The chef names what is low while looking along the shelves. The app turns that into lines from the kitchen's own guide, and anything that came out wrong gets fixed on screen before it is sent.
bullets: Every line is approved by the kitchen before it goes
Open for orders 24/7, at midnight as easily as noon
Runs on the iPhone or Android phone already in their pocket
Saves 20 to 30 minutes compared with the same order by phone
Interrupted by a delivery? The order waits where they stopped

rows.h3: Guides built from a file you can already export
rows.body: Export what each account usually orders, with your product codes and that account's prices, and we load it as the kitchen's guide. Your full item list stays in Acumatica; a guide holds just the items one kitchen orders.
bullets: Kitchens see their own items and nothing else
Prices and guide contents are yours to set
Change a guide in our admin platform whenever your prices move

rows.h3: Emailed, or sent by EDI or the API
rows.body: A finished order arrives by email as a PDF, Excel or Word file, or travels by EDI, by API or into QuickBooks. By email, your team keys it in from a list the chef already approved, not from a voicemail. We go through which of these your Acumatica setup can take straight in during the demo.
bullets: Goes to a shared inbox or straight to a rep
Over EDI or the API, when your setup takes it, nobody retypes it
Picking, shipping and invoicing run as they do now
No module to turn off before you begin

rows.h3: Incoming orders with stock levels beside them
rows.body: VoiceOrder Solutions gives real-time inventory visibility tied to order activity. It does not replace your stock system: that stays in charge, and a demo shows how the levels connect.
bullets: Fewer stockout surprises on a large order sent late
The catalog updates as your stock levels change

Lots, counts and replenishment stay with Acumatica

cards.h2: Where Acumatica ends and VoiceOrder Solutions begins
cards.lead: The portal and our app run in parallel, so this is not an alternative to Acumatica. A kitchen builds its order with us, and the work after that happens in Acumatica.

items.body: Once a kitchen's app order is in Acumatica, it still checks the customer's credit limit before releasing it, as it does for any order. Customer records, stock and invoicing remain there too. On our side sit each kitchen's guide and its prices, which you edit yourself, plus a copy of the orders chefs send with the app.

items.h3: Kitchens on the portal stay there
items.body: A kitchen content with the Acumatica portal keeps its login and goes on ordering there. The app is for the ones who call instead, and an order a chef sends from it carries our order number and time stamp, which a call never gets.

items.h3: Acumatica's app stays with your staff
items.body: Acumatica's own mobile app is made for your staff, who use it for sales orders and approvals. Ours goes on the kitchen's phone for one job only: getting the chef's reviewed order to you.

midcta.h3: See what a kitchen that never logs in would send you
midcta.body: Twenty minutes: a chef's list is spoken into the app, checked, then sent, and we show how it would reach a team that runs Acumatica.

steps.h2: From your export to a kitchen's first order
steps.lead: Setup happens outside Acumatica, in three steps.

items.h3: Guides go live, account by account

items.h3: Checked orders land with your team

comparison.h2: Acumatica runs the business. Kitchens get one more way in.
h2_lines: Kitchens get one more way in.

Acumatica still runs the stock, the money and the warehouse, so those rows hold true with or without us. An Acumatica alternative would mean changing ERPs; this is not one, and nothing wires the two together.

faq.h2: What Acumatica users ask before a demo

items.q: Do we need an Acumatica alternative before kitchens can place spoken orders?
items.a: No. Keep Acumatica and its portal running, and hand our app to the chefs who pick the phone over a login. Acumatica still handles the money, the stock and the credit checks; the app lets those callers send a checked order without dialing.

items.q: Acumatica does not charge per user seat. Why not just give every kitchen a portal login?
items.a: You can, and for kitchens that like to shop online it works well: live stock, their own prices, past orders to repeat. The gap is the kitchen that will not sit down to browse. For that kitchen, we offer a way to say what it needs instead.

items.q: Is talking an order through better than Acumatica's portal?
items.a: For the kitchens that keep calling instead of logging in, yes: saying the order and checking each line suits them better than browsing a catalog and checking out. For kitchens happy in the portal, keep the portal. Either way, nothing moves out of Acumatica; our app sits alongside it and is not an Acumatica alternative.

items.q: Does anyone else sell voice add-ons for Acumatica?
items.a: Yes. Some add-ons let reps dictate orders. Others answer a customer's call and record what is ordered. Ours puts the app in the kitchen's hands, and the kitchen confirms every line before it reaches you.

items.q: Will orders flow into Acumatica on their own?
items.a: Nothing links them out of the box: they are two products from two companies, and each company's support covers its own product only. Over EDI or through the API, the order may load straight into Acumatica without being typed again, if your system is set up to accept it; we check that in the demo. By email, you get a file the chef has already gone over, and your team enters it from that, not from a call or a voicemail.

items.q: Does our Acumatica partner have to be involved?
items.a: Not to get started. Setup takes no Acumatica login and puts nothing inside it: we work from a spreadsheet you export. If orders should later import on their own, we cover in the demo what you would have to arrange.

items.q: How quickly could kitchens start, and what is the cost?
items.a: Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours, since nothing changes inside Acumatica. On price, Acumatica publishes a starting figure for its distribution package; we publish none and quote per distributor. An Acumatica replacement would shift your accounting, inventory and warehouse onto a new ERP, which is a different decision from adding an ordering app.

items.q: Where did these Acumatica facts come from?
items.a: We checked acumatica.com and Acumatica's community site on 9 November 2026, looking at the distribution pages, the customer portal and its datasheet, the pricing and distribution package pages, the AI page and the AI Assistant notes. Their prices and results figures are left off this page. Should a detail have changed since, send us a note and we will correct it.
